name: Hollow
subtitle: the shy ghosts
story: The ghosts on Hollow are shy. They live in wardrobes and under the stairs, and if you say boo they faint, which is awkward for everyone. At the end of October the living go door to door to apologise for the year's frights. The ghosts leave sweets out on the step to say it's fine, really.
hook: A planet for people who say sorry to furniture.
beats: The ghosts on Hollow are shy. Say boo and they faint.
So at the end of October, the living go door to door to apologise.
odd_line: Please don't say boo near the ghosts. It takes them an hour to come round.
question: What's the last thing you apologised to?
extra: The haunted house tour is mostly people whispering sorry into cupboards.
reel_lines: The ghosts on Hollow are shy. Say boo and they faint.
So at the end of October, the living go door to door to apologise.

beats.text:
Hollow's ghosts are shy.
They take an hour to come round.
Bump a wardrobe, you say sorry. It might be occupied.

Every October, on Sorry Night,
the living go
wardrobe to wardrobe.
Mo, 9, has a list. Slammed doors. One boo, by accident. The recorder.
Mo's doing the whole street.

By morning there are sweets
on every step. Cold ones.
Mo has already written back. 'Sorry for the trouble.'

episode.end: For people who apologise to furniture.
episode.caption:
Who's that standing by the ghost?

Hollow has 4,000 living residents. The other kind won't come out to be counted. They keep to wardrobes, airing cupboards and the space under the stairs, and a sneeze can floor one. Saying boo needs written consent. One lives in the school piano, so lessons are recorder only.

Sorry Night is the last night of October: knock on each wardrobe once, softly, say what you did, and go. Mo got the most sweets on the street. Nobody's sure what that says about the recorder.

On Earth, one root of Halloween door-knocking is souling: in medieval Britain the poor went house to house at Hallowtide and were given soul cakes for praying for the household's dead. On Hollow the living knock, and the dead hand out the treats.

What's the last thing you apologised to?

short.title:
You've just said boo
to a ghost.

beats.text:
It takes an hour to come round.
You should apologise.

Nudge a wardrobe? Say sorry.
It might be occupied.

name: Lantern
subtitle: the pumpkin coast
story: Pumpkins on Lantern grow as big as garden sheds and glow from the inside from September until the first frost. Fishing boats steer home by them. Every family carves a face into theirs, so the boats know whose house they're passing.
hook: A planet for people who leave the porch light on.
beats: Pumpkins grow as big as sheds here and glow from the inside all autumn.
Every family carves a face into theirs, so the boats coming home know whose house it is.
odd_line: Lighthouse budget: none. Pumpkin budget: considerable.
rule: Do not carve a frightening face. The boats get nervous.
question: What face would you carve?
extra: The biggest pumpkin this year has its own postcode.
reel_lines: Pumpkins grow as big as sheds here and glow from the inside all autumn.
Every family carves a face into theirs, so the boats coming home know whose house it is.

episode.opener:
Every pumpkin on Lantern
is waiting for someone.

beats.text:
Each family carves its own face,
so the boats know
whose house they're passing.
Never carve a frightening face. The boats get nervous.

When the boats come in,
the pumpkins go out,
house by house.
Dark means everyone's home.

All but Mrs Penhale's.
Her son moved away
twelve years ago.

He rings every Sunday.
Pumpkins don't count phone calls.

He came in at two.
The pumpkin went dark
at five past.

episode.caption:
Watch the pumpkin by the lighthouse.

Lantern is a fishing coast of 62,000 people, with two moons, a twenty-hour day and no streetlights. Pumpkins grow on the hills above every harbour, as big as garden sheds, and glow from September until the first frost. The fleet steers home by them, which makes the lighthouse mostly ceremonial. This year's biggest has its own postcode. Mrs Penhale keeps the lighthouse, and every autumn she carves the face Jory drew for her as a boy. I lodged with her that week. If I stayed out late, the whole coast knew.

On Earth, the last Thursday of October is Punkie Night in Hinton St George, Somerset: the story goes that the village men stayed too long at Chiselborough fair, so their wives carved lanterns out of mangelwurzels and went to fetch them home. On Lantern, the lanterns stay home and wait.

What face would you carve?

first_comment: Mrs Penhale's pumpkin was lit again this evening. Jory's gone to the pub.

short.title:
The boats here
steer by pumpkin.
short.sub:
For anyone who leaves
the porch light on.

beats.text:
Never carve a scary face.
The boats get nervous.

When the boats come in,
the pumpkins go out.

name: Mothwing
subtitle: the light-eating moths
story: The moths on Mothwing have wingspans like kites, and they live on light. Each night they lift the moonlight off the fields and carry it back up. Leave a candle in the window and they'll take that too, but they leave a little glowing dust on the sill, which lasts until morning.
hook: A planet for people who pretend to be out on Halloween.
beats: The moths here are the size of kites, and they eat light.
Leave a candle out and they'll take it. They leave a little glowing dust as a thank you.
odd_line: Missing: one candle. Found: a small pile of glowing dust.
rule: Candles left out after dark are considered a donation.
question: Would you leave a candle out?
extra: They're very polite about it. They always leave the wick.
reel_lines: The moths here are the size of kites, and they eat light.
Leave a candle out and they'll take it. They leave a little glowing dust as a thank you.

beats.text: Moths. The size of kites.

Leave a candle out
and your moth will take it.

They're very polite about it.
They always leave the wick.

Everyone leaves one out.
Not Gordon.
He says he's not made of candles.

His moth sat on the roof all night,
looking in.

It wasn't cross.
Just disappointed.
Now Gordon leaves out thirteen.

episode.end: Your moth is on the roof tonight.
episode.caption:
Mothwing has 19,000 people, two moons and a 36-hour day, so the nights run to eighteen hours and the moths are never short of work. They have wingspans like kites and live on light. Every night they lift the moonlight off the fields and carry it back up, and each one keeps the same round of windows all its life. A candle left on the sill after dark counts as a donation. They take the flame, leave the wick, and leave a little glowing dust that lasts until breakfast. Nobody sells nightlights. There'd be no point.

Nobody has ever been hurt by one. Several people have been made to feel terrible.

I left a torch out on my first night, to be helpful. I got it back. Switched off.

What does your family say they're not made of?

first_comment: Gordon would like it known that he is still not made of candles. He has ordered more.

short.title:
The moths here
eat moonlight.
short.sub:
Everyone leaves them a candle.
Except Gordon.

beats.text:
So his moth sat on the roof
all night, looking in.

It wasn't cross.
Just disappointed.

short.end: Now Gordon leaves out a spare moon.
